name: Power

sections.body: Power is still a grid problem: generate, store, and wire. The fantasy change is what is allowed to make current. A sietch runs on desert sun, open-air turbines, a rare vent, or expensive fusion — not on chopped wood or a river that Arrakis does not have.
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: Wiring and lights stay Core hardware so stoves, smithies, and pumps keep working. Conduits become power leads, lamps become glowglobes, and the Electricity project is still the unlock — now named sietch electrics. Waterproof cable is hidden because standing water is not the Arrakis story.
sections.title: Leads and glowglobes

sections.body: Everyday current is compact sun-cells and sand turbines. Larger arrays and turbine arrays are the industrial step. Fusion is the late constant plant: no fuel item, no daylight, expensive enough that sun and wind remain the ordinary path. Sand turbines use the same open-air siting as windtraps, but they make electricity, not water.
sections.title: Sun, wind, fusion

sections.body: Household storage is the Core battery converted in place: a plasteel fuel-cell that still shorts in the rain. Keeping the vanilla DefName means quests, alerts, and DLC that mention batteries continue to function.
sections.title: Fuel-cells

sections.body: A steam vent is a jackpot, not a common water building. Capping it takes both current and a large flow of sealed rations. Windtraps remain how a sietch drinks on ordinary days. How often vents appear on the map is still a later geology pass.
sections.title: Deep vents

patches.purpose: Converts grid/lights and hides Core temperate producers

summary: Arrakis keeps RimWorld's power net — sealed leads, switches, and glowglobes — and replaces wood fires, river wheels, and chemfuel plants with sun, wind, rare vents, and late fusion.
